items.abstract: Functional MRI (fMRI) has traditionally focused on grey matter activations, overlooking the contribution of white matter pathways to brain organisation. Yet evidence suggests that white matter constrains, modulates, and integrates signals across distant regions. Here, we introduce a framework to map the functional specialisation of white matter circuits using fMRI scans collected while participants watched naturalistic videos. By leveraging ecologically valid stimuli, this method captures cognition as it naturally unfolds. Integrating fMRI with brain connections, we derived a functionally grounded parcellation of the connectome, challenging conventional cortical-based cognitive taxonomy. Distinct cognitive profiles emerged for association and commissural fibres, with association pathways preferentially linked to language-related processes and commissural pathways to executive and motor functions, affirming the functionally heterogeneous nature of white matter systems. An artificial intelligence framework applied to independent datasets confirmed the robustness and functional relevance of the identified parcels. This open-access framework also enables the interactive exploration of white matter functional organisation, offering a new lens on the neural bases of cognition.

items.title: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event.
items.last_author_affiliation: Climate and Environmental Physics, Physics Institute, University of Bern, Bern, Switzerland.; Oeschger Centre for Climate Change Research, University of Bern, Bern, Switzerland.
items.abstract: In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Here, we apply ensemble boosting to a coupled Earth system model to generate physically consistent alternative evolutions of a 2023-like event. The boosted ensemble produced marine heatwaves lasting up to 579 days, reaching maximum intensities of 4.5 °C above climatology and cumulative intensities of 717 °C·days, compared with 240 days, 2.9 °C and 224 °C·days in observations. Detailed analyses of the longest and most intense events highlight contrasting roles for persistent Euro-Atlantic high pressure, reduced turbulent heat loss, enhanced shortwave radiation and upper-ocean heat redistribution. Finally, we place these present-day storylines in the context of future warming, showing that events comparable to the observed 2023 event become increasingly common as global warming progresses.

items.title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation.
items.last_author_affiliation: RIKEN SPring-8 Center, 1-1-1 Kouto, Sayo-cho, Japan.
items.abstract: Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)-a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process-has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

items.title: A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo.
items.last_author_affiliation: Stanford University, 1651 Page Mill Road, Palo Alto, CA, USA. sheltzer@stanford.edu.
items.abstract: The cyclin-dependent kinase CDK11 is an understudied kinase that has been the subject of conflicting reports regarding its function in cancer. Here, we combine genetic and pharmacological approaches to demonstrate that CDK11 is a critical regulator of cancer cell survival that is required for RNA splicing and the expression of homologous recombination genes. Inhibition of CDK11 disrupts genome stability, promotes the retention of intronic sequences in mature mRNAs, and induces synthetic lethality with PARP inhibitors. Through integrative analysis of functional genomics datasets, we identify heterozygous deletions of chromosome 1p36 - which encompasses CDK11 and its activating cyclin CCNL2 - as a recurrent and predictive biomarker of sensitivity to CDK11 inhibition. To assess the therapeutic potential of CDK11, we establish a genetically-engineered mouse model that allows us to differentiate between the on-target and off-target effects of CDK11 inhibitors in vivo. Using this platform, we demonstrate that MEL-495R, an orally bioavailable CDK11 inhibitor, induces widespread on-target toxicity, revealing a narrow therapeutic index. Experiments with a chemically distinct CDK11 inhibitor similarly reveal minimal anti-cancer activity at tolerable doses. Together, these findings define CDK11 as a core cancer dependency, uncover a chromosomal deletion that sensitizes tumors to CDK11 inhibition, demonstrate that on-target toxicity limits the efficacy of CDK11-targeting therapies, and provide a generalizable strategy for deconvolving drug efficacy and toxicity in vivo for novel oncology targets.

items.title: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases, Emory University, Atlanta, GA, USA. eleanor.varian.thomas@emory.edu.; Department of Neurology, Emory University, Atlanta, GA, USA. eleanor.varian.thomas@emory.edu.
items.abstract: Predictive biomarkers are increasingly used to guide clinical trial design, diagnosis, and management of patients with neurodegenerative diseases. We profiled plasma from 632 ALS patients and 160 healthy controls using the NULISA CNS and Inflammation Panels and applied eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with nested cross-validation and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify disease-associated proteins. A 12-protein candidate panel was refined using SHAP feature importance and absolute quantification, then evaluated in an independent validation cohort (144 ALS, 37 controls). We identified a final 10-protein panel (NEFL, FOLR1, pTau-181, TREM1, VEGFA, NEFH, CALCA, NRGN, LAMP3, and PTX3) that achieved high classification performance (balanced accuracy 98.3%; AUC 0.992). Model performance was driven by plasma proteomic signatures rather than clinical variables and was not dependent on neurofilament light chain alone. Representing over 750 ALS cases, this study supports development of a clinically deployable blood-based ALS screening tool.

items.title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins.
items.last_author_affiliation: Flow Chemistry Group, van't Hoff Institute for Molecular Sciences (HIMS), Universiteit van Amsterdam (UvA), 1098 XH, Amsterdam, The Netherlands. t.noel@uva.nl.
items.abstract: Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

items.title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China. yamei_yu@scu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. In this study, we characterize two bacterial defense systems: TFAD1 featuring a serine protease and TFAD2 featuring a Ser/Thr kinase. We show that TFAD1 and TFAD2 act on phage long tail fiber proteins via protein degradation and phosphorylation, respectively. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny-a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term "passive Abi". Our findings expand the paradigm of bacterial immunity by unveiling protease- and kinase-mediated incapacitation of phage structural proteins, offering insights into the molecular arms race between bacteria and phages.

items.title: Balancing the Performance Trade-off of Polymer Blends with Heterogeneously Dispersed Nanodomains via Reactive Processing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Organosilicon Chemistry and Material Technology, Ministry of Education, Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Organosilicon Material Technology, College of Material, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Hangzhou Normal University, 311121, Hangzhou, China. yongjin-li@hznu.edu.cn.; Zhejiang-South Africa Joint Laboratory of Sustainable Polymer Composite Materials and Technology, Hangzhou Normal University, Hangzhou, 311121, China. yongjin-li@hznu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale.

items.title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization.
items.last_author_affiliation: Universität Münster, Organisch-Chemisches Institut, Münster, Germany. fernandg@uni-muenster.de.
items.abstract: Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing-an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid-liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

items.title: Alkali hydrides catalyze hydrogenolysis of polystyrene to alkylbenzenes under mild conditions.
items.last_author_affiliation: Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Dalian, China. pchen@dicp.ac.cn.; Center of Materials and Optoelectronics Engineering, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. pchen@dicp.ac.cn.
items.abstract: This study introduces a highly efficient, transition-metal-free method for upcycling polystyrene (PS) waste using alkali metal hydrides, specifically KH, as a catalyst. Operating under mild conditions (130 °C, 1 bar H₂, 3 hours), KH achieves an impressive 93.2% yield of gaseous products and alkylbenzenes, with 95.8% selectivity toward alkylbenzenes. The production rate of 313.3 mmolcarbon/gKH/h is approximately 2.6 times higher than noble-metal catalysts operating at much higher temperatures (280 °C). This versatile approach is effective on diverse real-life PS waste. Mechanistically, depolymerization is driven by a synergy between direct hydride-induced Hδ+(C) abstraction and K+···π interactions with adjacent phenyl rings. This interaction elongates the C(sp³)-C(sp³) bonds, facilitating targeted cleavage into alkylbenzenes. Ultimately, this work establishes hydride catalysis as an energy-efficient platform for plastic depolymerization, providing crucial insights for designing mild-condition catalysts to address the global plastic waste crisis.

items.title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
items.last_author_affiliation: Stanford Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences, SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, CA, USA. jostd@stanford.edu.; Linac Coherent Light Source, SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, CA, USA. jostd@stanford.edu.
items.abstract: Understanding the excitations of quantum materials is essential for unraveling how their microscopic constituents interact. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. Here we report its direct observation in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. We resolve a linearly dispersing excitation with velocity comparable to the Fermi velocity and find quantitative agreement with simulations of the non-interacting charge susceptibility. A detailed analysis and decomposition of the simulations reveal the intra-band origin of this low-energy excitation, confirming it as the Lindhard continuum. Our results establish ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering as a momentum-resolved probe of the fermiology in metals.

items.title: Discovering network resilience formulas with symbolized reinforcement learning.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Electronic Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. liyong07@tsinghua.edu.cn.; Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. liyong07@tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Many complex networks display remarkable resilience under external perturbations, internal failures and environmental changes, yet they can swiftly deteriorate into dysfunction upon the removal of a few keystone nodes. Discovering formulas that measure network resilience offers the potential to prevent catastrophic collapses-from species extinctions to financial crises-with profound implications for real-world systems. Existing resilience metrics are typically designed to characterize topological properties, whereas in many real systems resilience is defined by the dynamics imposed on the network; consequently, metrics that explicitly incorporate dynamical state information are expected to be better suited for identifying keystone nodes in such settings. Here, we report an automatic method for resilience metric discovery, which learns from how machine learning model solves a complicated network dismantling problem and symbolizes its network attack strategies into mathematical formulas. This proposed self-inductive approach discovers a resilience formula that accounts for both topology and dynamics, highlighting how the correlation between node degree and state shapes overall network resilience. Additionally, our approach discovers formulas that refine existing well-established resilience metrics with over 37.5% improvement in accuracy, significantly advancing human understanding of complex networks with machine learning.

items.title: Towards scalable DNA data storage with DNA-SaM codec system.
items.last_author_affiliation: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. huangxl@siat.ac.cn.; Shenzhen Key Laboratory of Synthetic Genomics, Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Synthetic Genomics, Key Laboratory of Quantitative Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen Institute of Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen, China. huangxl@siat.ac.cn.; Hubei Hongshan Laboratory, Wuhan, Hubei, China. huangxl@siat.ac.cn.; College of Informatics, Huazhong Agricultural University, Wuhan, China. huangxl@siat.ac.cn.
items.abstract: The exponential growth of global data volume is driving an urgent need for novel storage medium. Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA), nature's genetic repository, presents a transformative solution with data storage density and lifespan orders of magnitude higher than conventional media. However, scaling DNA storage has been hindered by the complexity of codec algorithms, the generation of biochemically problematic sequences, and the absence of robust architecture for large-scale data. We present DNA-SaM, a system integrating highly efficient encoding, stringent biochemical constraint checks, and a storage unit distribution paradigm facilitated by a two-tiered indexing architecture. DNA-SaM demonstrates linear encoding time complexity and substantially reduced encoding time compared with representative approaches by in silico analysis. Critically, it proactively excludes sequences such as homopolymer runs, tandem repeats, and potential promoter motifs that could interfere with downstream biochemical processes, showing improved compatibility with in vitro and in vivo applications. It is further validated by practical data storage both in vitro and in vivo with a 100% success rate. On the basis of its encoding scheme and sequence design space, DNA-SaM could theoretically store data exceeding 270 petabytes (PB), marking an advancement in the scalability of DNA-based data storage.

items.title: Production of abundant defective viral genomes by an insect-specific alphavirus revealed by nanopore sequencing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Infectious Diseases and Public Health, Jockey Club College of Veterinary Medicine and Life Sciences, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China. runsheng.li@cityu.edu.hk.; Department of Precision Diagnostic and Therapeutic Technology, City University of Hong Kong Shenzhen Matter Science Research Institute (Futian), Shenzhen, China. runsheng.li@cityu.edu.hk.; Tung Biomedical Sciences Centre, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China. runsheng.li@cityu.edu.hk.
items.abstract: Defective viral genomes (DVGs) shape virus-host interactions and evolution, yet remain poorly characterized in insect-specific viruses. Using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS), we profile full-length RNA species of Eilat virus (EILV), a mosquito-restricted alphavirus. We found that EILV produces abundant deletion-type DVGs far exceeding those seen in related arboviruses under identical conditions. These DVGs retain intact terminal sequences with conserved junction motifs. A modified DRS approach reveals widespread premature termination during EILV genomic RNA synthesis, linking DVG formation to reduced replicase processivity. Notably, a subset of DVGs is selectively replicated and packaged, accumulating over serial passages and interfering with parental virus replication. Our findings uncover an intrinsic, high DVG-generating capacity in EILV, linking low-processivity RNA synthesis with increased genomic plasticity. This suggests that elevated DVG production may be an adaptive mechanism, providing important insights into alphavirus evolution and replication fidelity in insect-specific RNA viruses.

items.title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS.
items.last_author_affiliation: National Physical Laboratory, NiCE-MSI, London, UK. gustavo.trindade@npl.co.uk.
items.abstract: Many biologically important molecules are structural isomers that share the same molecular mass yet differ in shape, bonding and function. This creates an ambiguity for mass spectrometry imaging (MSI), where chemically distinct species can be indistinguishable on the mass-to-charge (m/z) scale and therefore cannot be reliably mapped in heterogeneous materials. Here we demonstrate that Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) can provide an orthogonal contrast that enables both identification and spatial separation of isomeric molecules directly on surfaces. By exploiting structure-dependent secondary-ion dissociation and gas-phase collisional effects during ion transmission, we discriminate isomeric trisaccharides raffinose, maltotriose and melezitose and spatially resolve raffinose and maltotriose in mixtures. We benchmark these measurements against ion mobility spectrometry and observe consistent trends between OrbiSIMS transmission behaviour and ion mobility separation. These results establish OrbiSIMS as an approach for isomer-resolved MSI at surfaces and interfaces, opening opportunities to map isomeric biomolecules in complex systems where spatial distribution is central to function.

items.title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Soil Pollution Control and Safety, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. shizhou@zju.edu.cn.; Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Agricultural Remote Sensing and Information Technology, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. shizhou@zju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004-2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

items.title: Short-term effectiveness and impact of Vaxchora vaccine during the 2024 cholera outbreak in Mayotte.
items.last_author_affiliation: Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Diseases Unit, Institut Pasteur, Université Paris Cité, INSERM U1332, CNRS UMR2000, Paris, France. simon.cauchemez@pasteur.fr.
items.abstract: Global cholera resurgence and vaccine shortage have driven the adoption of reactive one-dose strategies with killed oral cholera vaccines (OCVs). The live-attenuated vaccine CVD 103-HgR (Vaxchora) shows high efficacy in human challenge studies, but its real-world effectiveness in outbreaks is unknown. Here, we analyze the 2024 outbreak in Mayotte, focusing on Koungou village, which had high cholera incidence and vaccine uptake. We develop several stochastic models and calibrate them to daily cases by vaccination status. In total, 3354 individuals (71%) of Koungou's at-risk population (n = 4733) received CVD 103-HgR, and 77 cases were confirmed, with symptom onset between 19 April and 7 July 2024. At baseline, we estimate a basic reproduction number  R 0   of 1.5 (95% credible interval (CrI): 1.2, 1.9) and a CVD 103-HgR effectiveness in preventing cholera of 87% (95% CrI: 74, 99), remaining between 75% and 91% across scenarios. Counterfactual simulations estimate 536 (95% CrI: 240, 824) cases averted at baseline, with a range of point estimates from 152 to 1228 across sensitivity analyses. Rapid single-dose CVD 103-HgR deployment is associated with high effectiveness during a real‑world outbreak, with a substantial but more uncertain population impact, supporting the inclusion of live-attenuated OCVs in reactive strategies when necessary.

items.title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden.
items.abstract: Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315-579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9-20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9-35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO2 emissions by 94.3-258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

items.title: Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Biomedicine and Biotechnology, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen, China. min.guan@siat.ac.cn.; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. min.guan@siat.ac.cn.; Shenzhen Key Laboratory of Marine Biomaterials, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Shenzhen, China. min.guan@siat.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysregulation under nutrient stress disrupts bone homeostasis. Although acetate metabolism is linked to diabetes and alcoholism, its role in the skeletal complications of these conditions remains unknown. Here we identify acetyl-CoA synthetase 1 (ACSS1) as a key stress responder that mediates mitonuclear communication in bone marrow skeletal stem cells. ACSS1-driven rewiring of acetate metabolism impairs cellular metabolic flexibility, mitochondrial function, and osteogenesis. Mechanistically, nutrient excess from glucose, alcohol or acetate upregulates ACSS1 via a mitochondrial ROS activated integrated stress response-CEBPB pathway. Maladaptive ACSS1 accumulation enforces excessive acetyl-CoA production from either exogenous or glucose/ethanol-derived endogenous acetate, promoting mitochondrial protein hyperacetylation specifically inactivating ME2 via lysine 94 acetylation. This ACSS1-triggered ME2 inactivation disturbs the malate-aspartate shuttle, leading to a self-perpetuating cycle of redox imbalance and oxidative stress that exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and osteogenic impairment. Importantly, genetic deletion of Acss1 or AAV-delivered non-acetylatable ME2 mutant in osteoprogenitor cells restores mitochondrial resilience, osteogenic capacity, and bone formation, protecting against osteoporosis or osteonecrosis in male mouse models of type 2 diabetes and chronic alcohol consumption. These results unveil an essential role for ACSS1 in controlling metabolic flexibility and osteogenesis, identifying ACSS1 as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic stress-related bone disorders.

items.title: Superradiant charge density waves in a driven hybrid cavity-matter system.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute for Theoretical Physics, ETH Zürich, Zürich, Switzerland.
items.abstract: Optical cavities enable strong, long-range, light-matter interactions that drive collective ordering, such as superradiant self-organization in ultracold atomic gases. Extending these ideas to solid-state electron systems could enable continuous-wave optical control of electronic order, but is impeded by the mismatch between optical wavelengths and electronic length scales. Here, we propose a platform for realizing superradiant charge density waves in doped, driven transition-metal dichalcogenides coupled to an optical cavity. A nanoscale grating generates electric fields at large in-plane optical momenta, allowing cavity photons to couple efficiently to electronic density fluctuations through exciton-polaron processes. Using a linear-stability analysis, we determine the threshold for superradiant ordering and map out the driven phase diagram. We show that matching the grating periodicity to the enhanced electronic density fluctuations-such as those near Wigner crystallization-lowers the required pump intensity. Our results establish a route toward cavity-controlled electronic order in quantum materials.

items.title: Near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks for cancer phototherapy.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Chemistry, Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Singapore. zhaoyanli@ntu.edu.sg.
items.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. However, the phototherapeutic agents based on COFs are usually activated with ultraviolet and visible light, resulting in the limitation of deep-tissue phototherapy. Herein, we develop near-infrared-responsive COFs through elaborate design and synthesis of a thia-hexaphyrin building block, which feature well-aligned conjugation skeletons for the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photothermal effect upon 808 nm laser irradiation, outperforming conventional porphyrin-based COFs. This porous framework exhibits high phototherapeutic efficacy, leading to the tumor suppression for 4T1 tumors and CT26 tumors in female mouse model by inducing immunogenic cell death through phototherapy and triggering systemic anti-tumor immune responses.

items.title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, Boston University, Boston, MA, USA. bbs@bu.edu.; Department of Biomedical Engineering, Boston University, Boston, MA, USA. bbs@bu.edu.; Neurophotonics Center, Boston University, Boston, MA, USA. bbs@bu.edu.; Center for Systems Neuroscience, Boston University, Boston, MA, USA. bbs@bu.edu.; Photonics Center, Boston University, Boston, MA, USA. bbs@bu.edu.
items.abstract: Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of  > 3 mm2. LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components.

items.title: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Liver Surgery, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, Chengdu, Sichuan Province, China. wangwt@scu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (GC) are standard first-line treatment for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here we report BicureX (ChiCTR2300073023), a single-centre, open-label, single-arm phase II trial of cadonilimab, an anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, plus GC for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTC. Patients received up to eight combination cycles followed by cadonilimab maintenance. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1); secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Sixty-one patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 23.5 months, ORR was 55.7% (34/61; 95% confidence interval, 42.4-68.5%), meeting the prespecified Simon two-stage efficacy criterion. DCR was 85.2%, median DoR 6.1 months, PFS 8.0 months, and OS 15.6 months. Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 68.9% and grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in 18.0%; no death was adjudicated as treatment-related. Proteomics identified a post-hoc exploratory three-protein response-associated signal without significance after false discovery rate correction. These findings support further randomized evaluation.
items.type: Clinical Trial, Phase II; Journal Article

items.title: Long-lasting chromatin and transcriptional states shape the maintenance of memory ensembles
items.abstract: Memories of recent events are stored within minutes in neuronal ensembles in the hippocampus. Over days to weeks, these memories undergo consolidation, and later retrieval depends on reactivation of a subset of neurons within the ensemble. However, how transient experiences produce lasting molecular and cellular changes in hippocampal ensemble neurons remains unknown. Here, we profile the functional, transcriptional, and gene regulatory states of hippocampal memory ensemble neurons at single cell resolution across multiple remote timepoints following single trial contextual fear conditioning. We uncover long lasting, cell type specific chromatin and gene expression changes after learning that coincide with sustained shifts in synaptic plasticity. Within dentate gyrus granule ensembles, we identify a persistent chromatin transcriptional program that emerges in a subset of ensemble neurons and is marked by sustained expression of many synaptic genes. This transcriptional signature predicts which neurons will be reactivated during memory recall, suggesting that only a fraction of initial ensemble neurons maintains a molecular state supporting later reactivation. Regulatory elements associated with this persistent state are highly enriched for AP1 motifs, the cognate binding sites for Fos family transcription factors, even though FOS protein has long since decayed away. Instead, we detect long lasting FOSB binding at these elements, suggesting a mechanism by which the effects of immediate early gene driven transcription are extended beyond the initial induction window. FOSB is particularly enriched in ensemble neurons that maintain enduring gene expression changes, suggesting it sustains chromatin accessibility and prolonged transcription in neurons reactivatable during memory retrieval. Together, these findings identify molecular mechanisms underlying the maintenance, maturation, and evolution of hippocampal memory ensembles over time.

items.title: Transcriptomic and Lipidomic Profiling of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia Reveals TREM2-Dependent and -Independent Processes
items.abstract: TREM2 has been implicated in AD as a critical regulator of microglial functions and loss of function mutations in TREM2 increases one's risk of developing AD. Given the diverse functional roles of TREM2, we sought to unravel how it affects downstream pathways using human iPSC-derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) derived from TREM2 knockout (KO) and isogenic control lines and assessing the response to oligomeric amyloid-{beta} 42 (oA{beta}42). While previous studies have primarily used fibrillar A{beta}, we focused on microglial responses to oA{beta}42 given their disease relevance and potent cytotoxic effects. At baseline, we identified a set of TREM2-dependent genes, which corresponded to the DAM signature in mice and disease-associated signatures in humans. Additionally, loss of TREM2 resulted in increased expression of cholesterol biosynthesis genes. In response to oA{beta}42, we found that the transcriptional response was largely TREM2-independent and corresponded to a strong induction of inflammatory pathways, with TREM2 also being downregulated in control iMGLs. We identified subsets of genes and pathways that were unique to either control, such as mitochondrial DNA and RNA degradation, or TREM2 KO iMGLs, such as the senescence-associated secretory pathway and adipogenesis, suggesting some differences in gene expression driven by TREM2 in response to oA{beta}42. Given that the inflammatory response was TREM2-independent, we sought to identify signaling pathways that contributed to inflammation. Inhibition of toll-like receptor signaling significantly reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory genes and modestly increased expression of TREM2 and TREM2-dependent genes. Consistent with our transcriptional data, cytokine production and secretion in response to oA{beta}42 was significantly increased to similar levels in both controls and TREM2 KO iMGLs. Lipidomic profiling of microglia revealed that triglycerides and lactosylceramides were significantly increased in both control and TREM2 KO iMGLs in response to oA{beta}42. TREM2 KO iMGLs had decreased levels of BMPs and increased levels of cholesterol esters across all conditions, further highlighting a role for TREM2 in maintaining lipid homeostasis in microglia. Taken together, we describe genes, pathways, and lipids that are associated with TREM2 expression that likely influence microglial responses to oA{beta}42.

items.title: In the non-canonical NF-κB pathway, binding of the initiating kinase NIK to the pathway's target, p100, serves a nonenzymatic "licensing" role
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Biomolecular Sciences, The Weizmann Institute of Science, 7610001 Rehovot, Israel
items.abstract: The non-canonical NF-{kappa}B pathway plays pivotal roles in adaptive immunity. It is initiated by NIK-mediated phosphorylation of IKK1, which phosphorylates p100 and promotes processing of newly synthesized p100. However, IKK1 can also be activated by other kinases to mediate distinct functions. Why IKK1-induced p100 processing occurs efficiently downstream of NIK but not of other kinases is unknown. Here, we show that whereas pre-existing p100 can be phosphorylated by IKK1 without NIK, phosphorylation of newly synthesized p100 critically depends on additional non-enzymatic functions of NIK's C-terminal portion. NIK binds IKK1 and restrains its kinase activity, while its binding to p100 enhances p100 phosphorylation. Single-molecule FRET spectroscopy and XL-MS revealed that the C-terminal region of p100 adopts a folded-back conformation and undergoes structural rearrangement upon NIK binding, likely accounting for this enhancement. Thus, NIK not only initiates the pathway but also dictates its specificity through binding to its downstream substrate.

items.title: Development of synthetic genetic arrays for studying interactions between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Biomedicine, Department of Medical Biochemistry and Cell Biology, Sahlgrenska Academy, University of Gothenburg, 405 30 Gothenburg, Sweden
items.abstract: Mitochondria, the central axis of metabolism and energy transformation has emerged as a focal point for understanding the aging process and a plethora of human diseases. Yet, how the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes communicate is still unclear. This work aims to allow the analysis of such crosstalk by developing a genome-wide platform for studying genetic interactions between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. Using yeast as a model system in which mitochondrial homoplasmy and stable alterations in the mitochondrial genome can be generated by biolistic bombardment, we created a genome-wide library of yeast cells carrying nuclear deletions and temperature-sensitive mutations together with a superfolder-GFP reporter for the expression of the mitochondrial-encoded COX2 gene. Using this approach, we found links between nuclear-encoded processes and mitochondrial gene expression not previously anticipated, including a requirement for genes involved in MVB (multivesicular body) sorting/RIM signaling, vesicle trafficking/glycosylation, polarity, and peroxisome biogenesis, for maintaining mitochondrial COX2 expression. In contrast, defects in the autophagy machineries, ribosome biogenesis, and nuclear transcription and chromatin organization resulted in increased expression of COX2. While reduced COX2 expression correlated with a reduced expression of the nuclear-encoded TOM70 gene in mutants defect in mitochondrial functions, expression of the mitochondrial and nuclear genes responded differently to defects in cytoplasmic ribosome biogenesis and autophagy. When creating the COX2 expression library, we also found that cells devoid of mitochondrial DNA rely on the Rim101 signaling pathway, and many of its auxiliary regulatory factors, to maintain fitness. As mutations in the Rim101 signaling pathway also caused down-regulation of COX2 expression, it appears that Rim101 signaling is central for maintaining proper control of mitochondrial function. We believe the approach will allow for future genome-wide studies on how nuclear-encoded processes influence the translation, protein folding, and processing of mitochondria-encoded genes.

items.title: Single-molecule tracking in the psychrophile Psychrobacter cryohalolentis reveals heat-shock-induced changes in ClpX dynamics
items.abstract: Psychrophilic organisms display a series of physiological adaptations which enable them to thrive in cold environments, yet the dynamics of these processes in living cells remain largely unexplored. Here, we establish super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule tracking (SMT) in the cold-adapted bacterium Psychrobacter cryohalolentis, enabling the investigation of protein dynamics in vivo at high spatiotemporal resolution. For controlled expression of HaloTag fusions in this organism, we developed an inducible plasmid expression system based on a galactose-inducible promoter. As a proof of concept, we followed the AAA+ unfoldase ClpX during steady-state growth and heat shock. At 22 {degrees}C, ClpX diffused as a single population with a media apparent diffusion coefficient of 0.25 m2/s, suggesting that most molecules reside in large complexes. A shift to 32 {degrees}C, above the growth maximum of this strain, broadened the mobility distribution, increasing both slow and fast populations, and transiently redistributed ClpX towards the cell periphery. During recovery the fast population returned to baseline within 5 min, whereas the slow population remained elevated for at least 30 min, suggesting that the two populations reflect distinct processes. SMT in a psychrophilic bacterium thus opens new possibilities to study how cold-adapted microorganisms respond to environmental change at the molecular level.

items.title: Sidetrak: a de novo-designed miniprotein targets the kinesin-1 coiled-coil stalk to inhibit MAP7 binding and disrupt mitochondrial transport
items.abstract: The coiled-coil domains of cytoskeletal motors contain regulatory surfaces that offer largely unexploited targets for manipulating intracellular transport. The microtubule-associated protein MAP7 promotes kinesin-1 motor activity, binding a coiled-coil surface that overlaps the TPR docking site (TDS), a regulatory interface involved in autoinhibition. Starting from an AlphaFold3 model of this relatively feature-poor surface, we used BoltzGen to design Sidetrak, a 36-amino acid miniprotein that binds kinesin-1 with nanomolar affinity. Binding requires the TDS and is abolished by mutation of the predicted Sidetrak interface, supporting the modelled local geometry of the targeted coiled-coil region. Sidetrak inhibits MAP7 binding, reduces MAP7-dependent kinesin-1 recruitment to microtubules in cells and causes perinuclear redistribution of mitochondria, a kinesin-1 cargo. Sidetrak binds all three kinesin-1 heavy-chain paralogues, and quantitative interaction proteomics revealed selective association with endogenous kinesin-1 complexes and associated cargo adaptors. These findings demonstrate selective disruption of a motor-MAP interaction by a de novo-designed protein and highlight regulatory coiled-coil surfaces as targets for manipulating intracellular transport. Beyond providing a means to manipulate intracellular transport, this work illustrates the potential of de novo protein design to test structural models of protein interfaces and probe endogenous protein networks to uncover underlying cellular mechanisms.

items.title: Genetic nurture and shared environmental effects across cognitive, educational, and mental health outcomes
items.corresponding_institution: Social, Genetic and Developmental Psychiatry Centre, King's College London
items.abstract: Genetic nurture, in which parental genotype predicts offspring outcomes independent of offspring genotype, operates at the between-family level, corresponding to the shared environmental effect (C) in the classical twin design. Genetic nurture represents a portion of C captured by parental genotype. The link between genetic nurture and C has not been systematically quantified across multiple trait domains. Using 2559 families with genotyped parents and 6710 twin pairs, we estimated genetic nurture using polygenic scores (PGS) and C using the twin design for 40 educational, cognitive, and anthropometric outcomes from age 7 to 26, and for 8 psychopathology symptoms at age 26. Although genetic nurture effects were small, the largest effects were observed for educational outcomes, followed by cognitive abilities, and then psychopathology symptoms. C followed the same pattern. Across eight trait domains, the correlation between genetic nurture and C was 0.68. However, psychopathology outcomes also showed relatively low PGS prediction, which creates a ceiling for estimated genetic nurture. In proportion to PGS prediction, psychopathology showed as much genetic nurture as educational outcomes. Why does psychopathology show genetic nurture despite showing no C? Why is psychopathology PGS prediction so low? We suggest that nonadditive genetic variance could explain both.

items.title: A large-scale multi-omics study of cortical miRNA dysregulation in Alzheimer's disease
items.abstract: MicroRNAs regulate gene expression, but their roles in Alzheimer's disease pathology and downstream molecular changes remain incompletely characterized. We integrated cortical small RNA-sequencing data from seven datasets across six postmortem cohorts comprising 1,738 individuals with transcriptomic, proteomic, genetic, and single-nucleus data. Meta-analysis of 405 microRNAs identified 16 associated with advanced and four with intermediate neurofibrillary tangle pathology, with miR-132-3p significant in both comparisons. Five microRNAs (miR-132-3p, miR-212-3p, miR-212-5p, miR-146b-5p, miR-3200-3p) showed evidence of mediating associations between target mRNA and protein expression and tau pathology. Consensus co-expression network analysis linked the miR-132/212 family to opposing neuronal/synaptic and oligodendrocyte/myelination-related programmes. Mediated targets were enriched among tau-associated differentially expressed genes across glial cell types, particularly astrocytes. Inferred cell-type regulatory networks further highlighted miR-132-3p and miR-146b as recurrent hubs. These findings prioritize a restricted set of cortical microRNAs and associated neuronal and glial molecular programmes for mechanistic investigation in Alzheimer's disease.

items.title: The genetic regulation of thyroid hormones on immune and hematopoietic homeostasis: an integrative Mendelian randomization and colocalization study
items.corresponding_institution: School of Nursing and Midwifery, University of Cape Coast, Cape Coast, Ghana
items.abstract: Background: Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. Methods: We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effects of 25 genetically predicted hematological traits on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the UK Biobank. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were selected as instrumental variables and harmonized before analysis. Causal estimates were primarily obtained using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method and complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, simple mode, MR-PRESSO, and MR-robust adjusted profile score (MR-RAPS) analyses. Sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, reverse causality, and directionality. Significant findings were replicated using independent FinnGen summary statistics. Multivariable MR and Bayesian colocalization analyses were subsequently performed to investigate significant associations further. Results: Among the 25 hematological traits evaluated, eosinophil-related traits showed the strongest associations with hypothyroidism. Genetically predicted eosinophil counts were associated with an increased risk of hypothyroidism (odds ratio [OR] = 1.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11-1.42, P = 4.0E-04, FDR = 0.002), while combined eosinophil-basophil counts showed similar associations (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.10-1.40, P = 5.0E-04, FDR = 0.002). These findings were consistently replicated in FinnGen and remained significant after adjustment for basophil traits, body mass index, and C-reactive protein in multivariable MR analyses. No significant associations were observed for hyperthyroidism. Bayesian colocalization identified strong evidence of a shared genetic signal at the rs653178 locus on chromosome 12 (PP.H4 = 0.994). Conclusions: This study provides genetic evidence supporting a causal role for eosinophil-related traits in hypothyroidism susceptibility. The consistency of the findings across complementary Mendelian randomization approaches, independent replication, multivariable analyses, and colocalization strengthens the evidence that eosinophil-related immune mechanisms contribute to hypothyroidism susceptibility.

items.title: MetaboRx: R Shiny application for quality assessment and preprocessing of mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data
items.abstract: Introduction Metabolomics datasets offer deep insights into biological systems, yet the multi-step analytical workflow, from sample preparation through instrumental analysis, introduces unwanted variation. This variation, including signal drift and batch effects can confound true biological signals. Although rigorous quality control (QC) and data preprocessing are prerequisites for downstream analysis, existing workflows are often fragmented, time-consuming, and inaccessible to non-experts. Objectives To develop a user-friendly software tool for rapid quality assessment and rigorous preprocessing of metabolomics feature tables. Methods MetaboRx is an R Shiny application that integrates orthogonal quality metrics into a single workflow, enabling systematic and transparent evaluation of metabolomics data before and after preprocessing. The application identifies formatting errors and analytically unreliable features and provides flexible preprocessing and visualization options. Results MetaboRx is freely available at https://github.com/ETaylorLab/MetaboRx. Using a semi-targeted LC-MS metabolomics dataset from mouse plasma, perturbed with simulated low-quality data, we demonstrate how MetaboRx facilitates detection of data quality problems, reduces unwanted variation, and prepares data for downstream analysis. Conclusion MetaboRx streamlines metabolomics data quality assessment and preprocessing through an interactive and integrated workflow. The application may improve consistency and reproducibility in metabolomics studies by supporting informed preprocessing decisions and transparent reporting of QC outcomes prior to downstream analysis.

items.title: TS-Zarr: a cloud-optimized Zarr layout for viewing and analyzing biomedical time series
items.abstract: Background: Biomedical time series are recorded at high sampling rates for hours to days across tens to hundreds of channels. Each recording occupies gigabytes to terabytes of storage. FAIR data sharing requirements often place recordings in cloud storage. Visual analysis requires downsampling windows wider than a few seconds to the pixel width of the screen. Visualization tools therefore either read a local copy of the recording or query a dedicated resampling server in front of the data. Findings: We present TS-Zarr, a Zarr v3 layout for time series data. It stores the samples of each channel alongside a pyramid of summary statistics at progressively coarser levels. Zarr on cloud storage offers low-latency, high-throughput parallel reads. The layout lets a reader fetch only the channels and windows it needs. These targeted reads scale better than the same reads from HDF5 and EDF. Precomputed levels trade additional storage and error-bound signal transformation for faster and more scalable visual analysis that moves from the whole recording to narrow windows. As users grow and windows widen, precomputed reads from cloud storage scale beyond the point at which a resampling server fails. Conclusions: Precomputed levels let researchers visualize a recording without downloading a local copy or querying a dedicated resampling server. The time to read a view remains bounded as the window under view widens. Zarr on cloud storage also provides efficient, highly parallelizable, targeted reads of raw sample data for analysis.

items.title: Combined nelfinavir and cisplatin treatment promotes inflammatory signaling and immunogenic cell death in ovarian cancer cells
items.abstract: Platinum (Pt) based chemotherapy remains central to ovarian cancer (OC) treatment, but recurrent disease frequently develops Pt resistance and responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) links tumor cell killing to antitumor immunity; however, cisplatin (CDDP), widely used in OC, is an incomplete ICD inducer. We previously demonstrated that the HIV protease inhibitor nelfinavir (NFV) enhances CDDP induced OC cell death and promotes a lytic, pyroptosis associated phenotype. Here, we investigated whether NFV enhances the immunogenic consequences of CDDP treatment. RNA seq analysis of OC cells treated with CDDP, NFV, or their combination revealed enrichment of interferon (IFN) associated, cytoplasmic DNA sensing, inflammatory chemokine, and antigen presentation pathways following NFV containing treatments. NFV alone and CDDP plus NFV reduced mature Lamin A abundance and increased extranuclear double stranded DNA accumulation. Cytosolic fractionation and droplet digital PCR demonstrated increased cytosolic TP53 DNA, particularly following combined treatment. CDDP plus NFV increased STING and TBK1 phosphorylation, supporting engagement of the cGAS STING TBK1 signaling pathway. The combination enhanced release of inflammatory and ICD associated mediators, including HMGB1, IL18, and IFNbeta. Importantly, vaccination with CDDP plus NFV-treated murine ID8 OC cells protected immunocompetent female mice against subsequent live ID8 cell challenge, reducing tumor incidence and burden. In contrast, ID8 cells killed by freeze thaw-induced accidental necrosis provided no comparable protection. Collectively, these findings indicate that NFV enhances the immunogenic consequences of CDDP induced OC cell death, potentially involving cytoplasmic DNA accumulation and STING TBK1 signaling, and promotes protective antitumor immunity in vivo. These results support further investigation of NFV as a repurposed partner for Pt based chemotherapy and its potential combination with immunotherapy in OC.

items.title: Multiomic analysis of a pleural mesothelioma organoid biobank defines gene dependencies and therapeutic vulnerabilities
items.corresponding_institution: Cambridge Institute for Medical Research (CIMR), University of Cambridge, Cambridge, CB2 0XY, UK , Cambridge University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Cambridge
items.abstract: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) remains an incurable cancer with few effective therapeutic options and limited understanding of its targetable dependencies, owing in part to a scarcity of clinically relevant, scalable models. Here, we describe establishment of an annotated biobank of 26 patient-derived PM organoids that faithfully recapitulate the clinical, genomic and histopathological landscapes of their parent tumours, including driver mutations, copy-number alterations and mutational signatures. By integrating these organoid models with a complementary collection of low-passage primary PM cell lines, we generate a functional precision oncology platform for PM. Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 screening across 23 patient-derived PM models uncovered 1,150 core fitness genes, including 638 not shared with pan-cancer core essentials, highlighting critical requirements for proteostasis, DNA repair, RNA processing and cell-cycle control. Parallel profiling of 106 compounds across 36 PM models revealed broad therapeutic vulnerabilities in proteostasis, growth signalling and epigenetic regulation. Beyond these shared vulnerabilities, both screens uncovered genotype-specific dependencies and drug responses linked to recurrent PM alterations. This functional map of shared and genotype-specific dependencies establishes patient-derived organoids as a scalable platform for precision therapeutic discovery in pleural mesothelioma

items.title: CD38-NAMPT-p21 signaling promotes stress adaptation in CLL
items.abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most common adult leukemia in the United States, accounting for ~30% of new diagnoses and ~4,000 deaths annually. High CD38 expression is a well-established marker of poor prognosis, yet the mechanistic basis of CD38-mediated treatment failure has remained incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that CD38 functions not merely as a prognostic biomarker but as a metabolic and signaling regulator that equips CLL cells to withstand cytotoxic and hypoxic stress. Using MEC-1 cells engineered to express CD38, we identified a CD38-NAMPT-p21 survival axis that confers resistance to fludarabine and hypoxia. CD38 NADase activity promoted NAMPT upregulation and AKT activation and was associated with accumulation of cytoplasmic p21. This CD38-dependent phenotype was lost in cells expressing a catalytically inactive CD38 mutant and was also reversed by pharmacologic inhibition of NAMPT (FK866) or suppression of p21 (UC2288). Analysis of three independent single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets of primary CLL further showed that naturally occurring CD38-positive CLL cells exhibit increased NAMPT expression and related stress-response signaling. Analysis of larger primary CLL cohorts further linked NAMPT expression to AKT and hypoxia signatures, providing additional support for the relevance of this pathway in patient-derived CLL. Together, these findings identify CD38-NAMPT-p21 signaling as an important mechanism of stress adaptation in CLL and suggest that targeting NAD metabolism and p21-mediated survival pathways may represent a potential strategy for CD38-high disease.

items.title: CD3⁺CD4-CD8- (Double-Negative) T-cells Provide Inflammatory Signals That Influence Myeloid Cells and Enhance Survival in Glioblastoma
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains resistant to immunotherapy, in part because of a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. While investigating the consequences of conventional T-cell depletion in a murine glioma model, we unexpectedly identified a population of double-negative T-cells (DNTs; CD3CD4-CD8-) that persisted following combined depletion of CD4 and CD8 T-cells. DNT enrichment was associated with significantly prolonged survival and revealed a distinct inflammatory transcriptional program characterized by activation-associated gene expression. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses demonstrated extensive remodeling of the glioma myeloid compartment, including enrichment of inflammatory signaling pathways and reduced expression of immunosuppressive markers. In complementary human studies, unmodified healthy donor-derived DNTs suppressed glioma stem cell viability, enhanced macrophage phagocytic activity, and reduced expression of the inhibitory myeloid receptor LAIR1. Intracranial administration of these unmodified DNTs significantly prolonged survival compared with PanT cells in an orthotopic glioblastoma xenograft model.. Collectively, these findings identify DNTs as previously underappreciated regulators of glioblastoma immunity that exert antitumor effects through both direct tumor suppression and inflammatory remodeling of the glioma myeloid compartment. These results support further investigation of DNT-based cellular therapies for the treatment of glioblastoma.

items.title: B7-H3 Orchestrates Fibro-Immune Spatial Organisation in Pancreatic Cancer
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal cancers in the western world and is largely resistant to treatment. A major barrier to effective treatment is the highly desmoplastic and immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment, where the organisation of tumour, stromal and resident immune cells limit immune infiltration. B7-H3 (CD276) is an emerging immune checkpoint marker investigated in phase I and Ib/2 clinical trials in PDAC, yet its biological role within the tumour environment remains poorly understood. We performed an integrated multiscale spatial profiling study to map B7-H3 expression across regional and single-cell spatial contexts in treatment-naive resected human PDAC. Furthermore, we explored the B7-H3 landscape in the neoadjuvant setting. Our results demonstrate that B7-H3 is not simply overexpressed in cancer but may act as a spatial organiser of the PDAC microenvironment, associated with a transition from epithelial-intrinsic tumour architecture to fibro-inflammatory immune states that underpin immune suppression, aggressive disease and poor prognosis. This fibro-inflammatory state appears conserved within the neoadjuvant landscape.

items.title: Common early-life exposure of the colorectal epithelium to the microbiome-derived mutagen colibactin
items.abstract: Colibactin is a mutagen produced by bacterial strains in the colorectal microbiomes of some healthy people. It generates somatic mutations characterised by the mutational signatures SBS88 and ID18 in normal human colorectal epithelial cells in vivo. Increasing prevalence of colibactin mutagenesis during the 20th century is hypothesised to have caused recent international increases in early-onset colorectal cancer incidence. Here, we establish the early-life prevalence, timing, mutation burdens and distribution through the colon of colibactin mutagenesis by sequencing normal colorectal epithelial cell genomes to detect SBS88 and ID18 in 90 healthy and inflammatory bowel disease affected children and adolescents. Colibactin-induced mutagenesis was present in ~43%, with or without inflammatory bowel disease. It usually begins shortly after birth and ceases by age five years. Mutation burdens are higher in the left than right colon and show substantial variation, with some children displaying mutation burdens comparable to those of healthy non-exposed individuals greater than 60 years of age. The future public health implications of this common early life mutagen exposure will depend on clarification of its role in colorectal cancer causation.

items.title: Expanding the SEVA plasmid toolbox for tuneable control of gene expression in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
items.abstract: The use of cyanobacteria as biotechnological chasses is considered a key point in the circular economy due to their scarce growth requirements and its capacity of fixing atmospheric CO2. However, for obtaining the most of their potential, it is often necessary to count with tools that allow the modification of the genetic expression. In this work, we have characterized a molecular toolbox for reliable control of gene expression control through induction or repression in Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 using SEVA plasmids. Different inducible promoters showing a variety of dynamic range, strength and leakiness using GFP our YFP as reporter genes were assayed. On the other hand, we also evaluated the gene repression in cyanobacteria by using CRISPRi technology, which allows to repress the gene transcription in a targeted manner. Employing an inducible promoter, a new SEVA-dCas9 based vector was built for Synechocystis sp. PCC6803. The vector contains dCas9 (DNase-dead Cas9 nuclease) under the tightly regulated PBADRSW promoter, which combines a theophylline-responsive riboswitch with a rhamnose-inducible promoter. The sgRNA expression cassette is also encoded on the same plasmid, resulting in a compact, self-contained CRISPRi system that simplifies genetic implementation and enables targeted gene. As a proof of concept, we demonstrated that the system enables reversible knockdown of a chromosomally integrated eYFP reporter driven by the constitutive Pc223 promoter in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. These results provide new insights into the genomic strategies and available promoters and CRISPRi-SEVA plasmids for the industrial cyanobacteria Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 that would be valuable for further applications.

items.title: Persistent DNA damage reprograms the cutaneous microenvironment into a stress-responsive immunometabolic pro-pigmentary niche
items.abstract: Chronic ultraviolet (UV) exposure induces progressive pigmentary remodeling of the skin, yet how persistent DNA damage influences tissue-level responses remains poorly understood. Xeroderma pigmentosum complementation group C (XP-C), characterized by defective global genome nucleotide excision repair, provides a model to investigate these processes. Here, integrating chronic UVB irradiation of Xpc-deficient mice with spatial transcriptomics, multi-omics profiling, and functional analyses, we identify a coordinated multicellular response associated with persistent hyperpigmentation. UVB-exposed Xpc-deficient skin exhibited increased eumelanin accumulation, altered melanosome organization, enhanced melanosome transfer to keratinocytes, and regional melanocyte expansion. Proteomic, metabolomic, and kinomic analyses revealed coordinated alterations in inflammatory, cytoskeletal, redox, metabolic, and pigmentation-associated programs. Spatial transcriptomics further identified distinct keratinocyte states and inflammatory immune niches enriched in hyperpigmented regions, coinciding with increased melanocyte abundance and DNA damage. These findings suggest that pigmentary remodeling occurs within a spatially organized, stress-responsive immunometabolic tissue environment rather than reflecting melanocyte-intrinsic alterations alone. Analyses of human XP-C skin and XPC-deficient primary human melanocytes revealed overlapping pigmentation-associated, inflammatory, and cytoskeletal alterations, supporting the relevance of these observations to human disease. Together, our findings reveal a previously underappreciated relationship between persistent DNA damage and spatially coordinated multicellular remodeling, providing a framework for understanding how defective genome maintenance is associated with chronic pigmentary changes and altered tissue homeostasis. These findings may also offer insights into the mechanisms underlying common acquired hyperpigmentary disorders.

items.title: A normalization strategy for extreme proteome regulation reveals distinct targets of eIF4A1/2 and their inhibitor silvestrol
items.corresponding_institution: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), Heidelberg, Germany
items.abstract: Cells rapidly adjust protein synthesis in response to stress, signalling and drugs, often converging on the cell's translation machinery affecting the synthesis of multiple proteins simultaneously. Nascent proteome analysis, combining pulsed SILAC labelling with enrichment of newly synthesized proteins (NSPs), can measure these changes proteome-wide. However, quantitative proteomics relies on normalization methods that assume most proteins remain unchanged. When protein synthesis shifts globally, this assumption fails: normalization then erases the biological effect, whereas omitting it leads to misinterpretation of data. Since no approach has so far reliably preserved global changes in protein synthesis, we developed labelled protein ratio (LPR) normalization, which uses the ratio of newly synthesized to pre-existing protein in the global proteome as an internal scaling factor. Two SILAC benchmarks showed that this factor is accurate down to a few percent of labelled protein and recovers defined global differences, whereas twelve established normalization methods did not. Applied to cycloheximide treatment, LPR normalization revealed a 57% decrease in synthesis, which median normalization reported as balanced up- and down-regulation with spurious increases in multiple proteins. After depletion of the core translation initiation factor eIF4A1, LPR normalization uncovered a broad translational repression that median normalization largely masked, while eIF4A inhibition with silvestrol showed a divergent pattern, suggesting secondary effects. LPR normalization thus provides a general strategy for quantifying global changes in protein synthesis.

items.title: Developmental emergence of cue-specific fear memory parallels maturation of prefrontal-amygdala circuitry in mice
items.abstract: Fear memories formed in early life are forgotten rapidly, but the circuits that delay stable memory expression are not well defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) projects to the basolateral amygdala (BLA), and both regions mature late, yet the behavior, anatomy and physiology of this pathway have rarely been examined together across development. We trained mice in cued auditory fear conditioning at postnatal day (P) 14-15, P20-21 or P59-70 and tested tone-evoked freezing 1, 7 and 14 days later. Early juvenile mice showed no cue-specific freezing at any memory retrieval time points, late juvenile mice showed it at 7 and 14 days but not at 1 day, and adults showed it at all retrieval time points. In separate mice, mPFC axons were low in the BLA at P11 and more abundant at P38 and P90, and light-evoked prelimbic synaptic responses in BLA principal neurons were not detectable at P11 but were robust at P35 and P70. Spontaneous synaptic currents and intrinsic excitability of BLA principal neurons, and excitability of prelimbic principal neurons and interneurons, also changed between P11 and adulthood. These data identify a protracted period of mPFC-BLA circuit maturation that overlaps the emergence of cue-specific fear and define the ages at which candidate mechanisms can be tested.

items.title: Endothelial VCAM1 links oncogenic KRAS signaling to myeloid inflammation and hemorrhagic instability in brain arteriovenous malformations
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic conversion is the most devastating complication of brain arteriovenous malformations (bAVMs). However, endothelial mechanisms promoting macrophages (M{varphi}) recruitment, microglia (MG) activation, and bAVM lesion instability remain unclear. We investigated vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM1) as a mediator linking oncogenic endothelial signaling to myeloid cell responses and hemorrhagic progression in bAVMs. METHODS: We performed integrated transcriptomic analysis of human bAVM and epilepsy-control brain tissues, with validation in local bAVM specimens. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of bAVM lesions and intact brain tissues from mutant KRAS-induced bAVM mice were followed by histological validation. Using AAV-BR1-KRASG12V-injected Cx3cr1-gfp;Ccr2-rfp mice, we performed intravital imaging to assess M{varphi}/MG responses to VCAM1 neutralization. Hemorrhage and myeloid cell responses were also evaluated following endothelial-specific VCAM1 deletion. Plasma soluble VCAM1 (sVCAM1) was measured in patients with unruptured and ruptured bAVMs and unruptured aneurysm controls. Effects of sVCAM1 on MG activation were examined in vitro. RESULTS: Integrated human endothelial bulk and single-cell RNA-sequencing and tissue validation identified VCAM1 upregulation in bAVMs, including unruptured lesions. Plasma analyses showed increased sVCAM1 in unruptured and ruptured bAVM patients compared with unruptured aneurysm controls. In mutant KRAS-induced bAVM mice, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses demonstrated increased VCAM1 expression, with endothelial localization confirmed histologically. In vitro, mutant KRAS increased sVCAM1 production, while recombinant sVCAM1 stimulated inflammatory mediator expression in MG. Both MG and M{varphi} expressed VLA-4, a major VCAM1 receptor. Intravital imaging showed that VCAM1 neutralization reduced M{varphi} accumulation and MG activation, while early VCAM1 neutralization reduced hemorrhagic burden. Consistently, endothelial-specific VCAM1 deletion reduced M{varphi} accumulation, MG activation, and hemorrhage volume in bAVM mice and improved behavioral performance. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify endothelial VCAM1 as an upstream mediator linking mutant KRAS signaling to myeloid cell responses and hemorrhagic progression in bAVMs. This study establishes endothelial VCAM1 as a potential therapeutic target for attenuating hemorrhagic progression.

items.title: Within-Subject Precision Measurement: Theory and Utility of Assessing Change Scores and Their Variance
items.abstract: Within-subject studies gain statistical power by removing stable between-subject differences from the comparison. However, the metrics commonly used to select measurement instruments and anticipate their within-subject performance are often based on between-subject correlations of raw scores from test-retest designs. Measuring each subject's change directly -- after an intervention, and ideally more than once -- provides a firmer basis for evaluating measurement precision and planning studies of within-subject change. Here we describe the statistical theory behind estimating measurement properties from change scores. In one instantiation, the pre- and post-intervention measurements are each made twice, yielding the duplicate change-score design. Such a design provides an estimate of the mean signal change and enables the decomposition of the total observed variance of change scores into true between-subject response heterogeneity and measurement noise. In extended designs, where multiple measures are collected within and across days, measurement noise can be further decomposed to distinguish within-session from between-day measurement variability. These estimates supply the inputs needed for within-subject study design, including providing a basis for selecting among alternative measurements and comparing processing pipelines, performing power calculations, and estimating the precision limits of detecting change within individual subjects.

items.title: Neural rosettes emerge from an interconnected tubular network in human cortical organoids
items.abstract: Cortical organoids generate multiple neural rosettes, self-organizing and radially arranged structures that resemble ventricular zones of the developing brain. Here, we show that these rosettes, commonly considered as discrete entities, originate from an interconnected tubular network. We demonstrate that the formation of this continuous structure involves neuroepithelial folding, invagination, and internalization, resembling aspects of neural tube formation.
